name: Arcturus Defense Solutions RCB-5 'Steadfast'
description:
The RCB-5 'Steadfast' is Arcturus Defense Solutions' workhorse riot control baton — the weapon that appears in more Meridian enforcement photographs, incident reports, and civil rights documentation than any other shock device in the city. First introduced in 2181 and now in its fifth hardware revision, the Steadfast has become the de facto standard for contracted security forces across Tiers 2 through 4, with Arcturus holding supply agreements with forty-seven distinct security contractors, transit authorities, and corporate facility operators. It is, in the most literal sense, the face of institutional enforcement in Meridian.

The Steadfast's design philosophy prioritizes durability and operator survivability over maximum discharge capacity. The baton's outer shell is a high-impact polymer rated to survive being run over by a standard transit vehicle, submerged in water for up to 30 minutes, and struck against concrete at full force without structural compromise. The discharge system delivers a consistent 150,000 volts — lower than many competitors — but Arcturus's engineering team has optimized the waveform for reliable neuromuscular disruption across a wide range of body masses, augmentation levels, and clothing thicknesses. The grip is contoured for extended one-hand carry and integrates a wrist retention lanyard mount as standard. Every unit logs discharge events with timestamp, duration, and charge level to a tamper-evident internal memory that Arcturus provides to contracted operators as part of their liability documentation package.

Civil rights organizations have a deeply ambivalent relationship with the Steadfast's discharge logging. On one hand, the logs have been used to hold operators accountable in documented abuse cases; on the other, Arcturus retains access to all discharge logs as part of its service agreement, creating a data collection architecture that critics describe as 'a comprehensive map of every enforcement action in Meridian, owned by a private defense contractor.'
legality: Licensed — standard enforcement tool; available to contracted security operators and licensed private security; discharge log requirement mandatory under Meridian Security Contractor Code 12-F
specifications:
Length: 60 cm
Weight: 0.88 kg
Discharge Voltage: 150,000 V
Discharge Waveform: ADS NMD-5 (neuromuscular optimized)
Battery Life: 100 strikes per power cell
Power Cell: ADS ProCell-3 (standard, widely available)
Shell Rating: IP67, impact-rated to 2-ton vehicle crush
Discharge Log: 2,000-event tamper-evident internal memory
Operating Temperature: -40°C to +70°C
Grip: Contoured polymer, lanyard mount integrated
Color Options: Standard grey, hi-vis yellow (transit variant)
tactical_use: The Steadfast is designed for sustained deployment in crowd-control and building-security contexts. Operators are trained in a four-position strike doctrine targeting the thighs, upper arms, torso, and — as a last resort — the head and neck. The baton's length and weight balance make it effective for both jabbing strikes and sweeping motions in tight corridor environments. In extended operations, operators appreciate the battery life and the robust construction, which eliminates the hesitation of using the weapon as a physical impact tool when the charge is depleted. The discharge log is a double-edged operational consideration: operators know their every deployment is recorded, which generally produces restraint but occasionally produces documentation that operators would prefer did not exist.
cultural_context: The Steadfast is simply called 'the blue rail' on the Shelf — a reference to the blue indicator light that glows when the baton is charged and ready. It is so ubiquitous that in Tier 1-2 communities, 'rail' has become a generic verb meaning to be struck by any shock baton, regardless of brand. The weapon's universality has made it a symbol of systemic enforcement in activist art and political discourse — it appears on murals, in music, and in protest insignia precisely because everyone knows what it is. Among security professionals, carrying a Steadfast without any personal modification is read as a sign of institutional loyalty or lack of individual initiative; operators who take pride in their work tend to upgrade.
known_users: virtually all Meridian contracted security forces
story_hooks: An analyst at an Arcturus data subsidiary has quietly noticed that the discharge log aggregation system — which maps every baton deployment across the city — shows a pattern: in the six weeks before every major Tier 1 protest or civil unrest event, deployment density in adjacent Tier 2 zones spikes dramatically, as if someone is using the logs to predict and preemptively suppress organizing activity. She has brought this to no one yet.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian riot control baton with a distinctly institutional aesthetic — angular, purposeful, designed to project authority rather than aggression. The form factor is deliberately unambiguous: a tool of enforcement, not a civilian object.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 60 cm (24 inches). Diameter at grip: approximately 3.2 cm. Grip section: 12 cm. Active strike head: conical, tapering from 2.8 cm to 1.4 cm point.
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and compact at 0.88 kg (1.9 lbs). Sits comfortably in extended one-hand carry without fatigue. Center of mass shifts toward the strike head during deployment, creating intuitive weight distribution for jabbing motions.
physical_description.primary_material: High-impact polymer composite rated for vehicle crush and submersion. Non-conductive for operator safety. Internal aluminum power cell housing and discharge grid.
physical_description.finish: Matte hard-coat polymer with subtle grip texture progression. Standard variant: institutional grey with minimal reflection. Hi-vis transit variant: fluorescent yellow with reflective striping at intervals.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: gunmetal grey or hi-vis yellow. Accent: black grip section with integrated silver lanyard attachment point. LED charging indicator (blue when ready, red during discharge cycle) recessed into pommel.
physical_description.grip_texture: Contoured polymer with deep crosshatch pattern — engineered for wet-hand retention and gloved operation. Slightly rubberized polymer overlay in critical contact zones. Lanyard retention loop (paracord-compatible) integrated at pommel.
distinctive_features: Recessed LED status indicator in pommel (blue/red charging state display)
Integrated lanyard retention loop — designed for quick-draw deployment from duty belt
Discharge grid visible through translucent panel on strike head — visible arc chamber confirms charge state
Manufacturer stamp on grip: 'ADS RCB-5 REV5.2' with serial number in raised lettering
Small maintenance port near base of grip (removable security plug for ProCell-3 swap)
Faint etching indicating strike zones at four positions along shaft
Impact-rated polymer shows minimal cosmetic wear but heavy operational scuffing typical of field use
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions logo (stylized 'A' with discharge arc motif) stamped on upper grip section. 'MERIDIAN CERTIFIED' and 'IP67' ratings laser-etched below. Serial plate recessed into pommel cap. Discharge log access port marked with Arcturus proprietary data connector.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but visibly deployed — minor impact scarring on strike head from contact with bodies and barriers. Grip polymer shows slight discoloration from extended field handling and sweat exposure. Lanyard loop shows wear from repeated deployment draws. No cosmetic corrosion (polymer prevents oxidation); battery indicator likely shows blue (ready state) on units in active rotation.
